tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y): The starting coordinates for `left_click_drag`.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). The canvas
   frozen on 2026-10-27 (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v)
   is history, not a source. Change the token file to match, or, when the
   code's value is the one to keep, change the artifact first. Do not trust
   old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

content.content:
# JusPrin design guidelines

**Status:** Canonical guidance for `jusprin-dev` on how a screen gets designed and checked, and on the words it shows. The visual system (tokens, type, color, components, logo) lives in [Design system](design-system.md); this document does not repeat it.

Design agents tend to write on-screen text that only they can read. The agent knows how the screen works, so a line like "The sixth digit signs you in." reads clearly to it and to any reviewer who knows the same. A person opening the app for the first time has to decode it, and often can't. The First-Launch Confusion Review (https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15, 2026-11-06) found 23 places on the first launch where a newcomer would misread or stall, and most of them were wording. The rules below exist to stop that at the source and to catch what still gets through.

## How a screen gets designed and checked

These steps apply to every change to text a person sees, not only to new screens: a new link on an existing board, a reworded line, or a one-sentence fix all get the cold-reader check on the board before building (step 5) and in the running app after (step 8).

1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those.
2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says.
3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board.
4. **Write every line by the wording rule below.**
5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.

## The cold-reader check

The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.

- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.

What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test.

## Wording

Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.

The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app.

1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses.
   - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had)
   - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it
2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for.
   - Before: "New or existing account, same door."
   - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it
   - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent)
   - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside.
   - Before: "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device."
   - After: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone."
4. **Internal labels.** A name the team uses, shown nowhere else on the screen, explains nothing.
   - Before: "An Expert message is 5 credits."
   - After: the cost in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent" (check the number against real costs)
5. **Hinting at a consequence instead of stating it.** If a choice changes what the person gets, say what it changes.
   - Before: "Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours."
   - After: "If you skip, files are sliced for a stand-in printer with a 250 mm bed, not for yours. Add your printer before you print anything. You can do that later on the home screen."

Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening.

Kenneth, 2026-10-21, on the calibration page I drew: "It looks like you didn't follow this hygiene. read design
guidelines in readme, and fix your own sloppiness", then "I suspect there were more sloppiness in the boards you
designed". He was right on both counts. I had copied markup from older canvas boards (the printer-menu board at
13 px rows, the stale ds-chat-reply-choice board) and from memory (a Home kebab with no Connect…, a black Remove,
a 220 px width, the filament menu in an old order), instead of from the two sources that are authoritative.

**Why:** rule 5 of "Writing UI code" (agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md) says the design system wins, and the
design system's truth is its coded bundle (`figma-mirror/published/ds/project/components/bundle.css`, classes
`.jp-*`), not any one board on the canvas: boards drift (the printer-menu board draws rows at 13 px, the reply
choice board draws the pre-capsule style). For surfaces the bundle has no component for (the printer receipt, a
sent photo in a message), the app's own CSS and TSX are the source.

**How to apply:** before drawing a board, dump the bundle rules for every component used (`grep '\.jp-<name>'

toolUseResult.stdout:
# JusPrin design guidelines

**Status:** Canonical guidance for `jusprin-dev` on how a screen gets designed and checked, and on the words it shows. The visual system (tokens, type, color, components, logo) lives in [Design system](design-system.md); this document does not repeat it.

Design agents tend to write on-screen text that only they can read. The agent knows how the screen works, so a line like "The sixth digit signs you in." reads clearly to it and to any reviewer who knows the same. A person opening the app for the first time has to decode it, and often can't. The First-Launch Confusion Review (https://claude.ai/artifact/91wmdS3QU8UkzbPi1zog15, 2026-11-06) found 23 places on the first launch where a newcomer would misread or stall, and most of them were wording. The rules below exist to stop that at the source and to catch what still gets through.

## How a screen gets designed and checked

These steps apply to every change to text a person sees, not only to new screens: a new link on an existing board, a reworded line, or a one-sentence fix all get the cold-reader check on the board before building (step 5) and in the running app after (step 8).

1. **Start from the person.** Before drawing, write down in two or three sentences who reaches this screen, what they know at that moment, what they came to do, and what they must decide here. Every line on the screen serves one of those.
2. **Draw the whole screen, not a component alone.** A board for review is the full screen at the app's size, with the header, panes and neighbouring content the person really sees there, on the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ). Build it from the Design System artifact's coded components and the app's own markup, never by copying an older board. Repeated compositions are imported by name, as [Design handoff requirements](design-system.md#design-handoff-requirements) rule 9 says.
3. **Fill it with real strings.** Text that summarises data comes from the rule that will produce it in the app, run on real data. If only a model could write a line, say so on the board.
4. **Write every line by the wording rule below.**
5. **Run the cold-reader check on the boards** (below). Rewrite and check again until every line and button reads as intended.
6. **Show the board for review by what a person sees.** Name the screen as the person would ("the welcome screen, after typing an email"), give the canvas page it is on, and attach the picture. Board ids and builder labels mean nothing to a reviewer.
7. **Build it** following [Writing UI code](design-system.md#writing-ui-code).
8. **Check it in the running app.** Take screenshots of the built screen along one real path and run the cold-reader check again. The guards prove the code went through the tokens; only the screenshots show what the person reads.

## The cold-reader check

The writer of a screen cannot see that its text is cryptic, so the check is done by a reader who knows nothing about how the screen works.

- Start a fresh agent. Give it only the screenshots and one or two sentences a real user would know (for example: "You own a 3D printer and just installed JusPrin, a desktop app that prepares 3D models for printing."). Give it no code, spec, design notes, chat history or list of suspected problems, and rename files so their names don't hint at anything.
- Use screenshots from one coherent path, in the order a person meets them. Mixing signed-in and signed-out screens, or states set by hand, makes the reader report contradictions that no user would see.
- Ask it, for each screen, to quote every line and every button exactly, say in one plain sentence what the line means or what the button will do, and list where it would hesitate, misread, worry, or not know what to do next, including information the screen leaves out. Tell it to read literally, like a busy newcomer: a line it had to puzzle out counts as a problem even if it worked it out.
- Compare its answers with the intent written in step 1. Any line it reads differently from the intent gets rewritten, however small the gap. Its other hesitations are input to weigh, not orders.

What the check is known to catch: on 2026-11-06 a fresh agent given only the review's ten screenshots fully caught 14 of the 23 problems and partly caught 4 more. It caught every cryptic phrasing in the list. It missed problems that need knowledge from outside the screen (that Skip installs a 250 mm Klipper printer) and finer editorial calls (a redundant reassurance, one allowance under three names, "Connected" used for an account). It also raised real questions the review had not, such as what happens after the free month. It has not been compared with a real first-time user, so for the screens that matter most, such as first launch, a person remains the final test.

## Wording

Every line says what the person does or what happens to them, in a full sentence, in words a newcomer already has.

The five patterns below are what the review found most. Each pair is the text the app showed and the review's proposed rewrite; the rewrites are proposals, not yet in the app.

1. **Facts joined by a middle dot.** The dot drops how the facts relate, and the reader guesses.
   - Before: "Signed in as new@example.com · 500 credits" (reads like a balance the person already had)
   - After: "You got 500 free credits for signing up.", with the email address on a smaller line under it
2. **Metaphors.** The reader has to work out what the image stands for.
   - Before: "New or existing account, same door."
   - After: a "Sign up free" button, with "Already have an account? Sign in" under it
   - Before: "Pick how the agent should think." (the options are ways to pay for or connect the agent)
   - After: "Sign up to use the AI agent, or skip it and just slice."
3. **Describing the mechanism instead of the action.** Say what the person does, not how the screen works inside.
   - Before: "The sixth digit signs you in. Read the email on any device."
   - After: "Type the code from the email. You can open it on your phone."
4. **Internal labels.** A name the team uses, shown nowhere else on the screen, explains nothing.
   - Before: "An Expert message is 5 credits."
   - After: the cost in things the person does, for example "500 credits is about 100 questions to the agent" (check the number against real costs)
5. **Hinting at a consequence instead of stating it.** If a choice changes what the person gets, say what it changes.
   - Before: "Skip, and JusPrin slices for a generic 0.4 mm printer until you add yours."
   - After: "If you skip, files are sliced for a stand-in printer with a 250 mm bed, not for yours. Add your printer before you print anything. You can do that later on the home screen."

Space on a screen is tight, and short text looks finished. That is how these lines get written. Shorten only after the full sentence passes the cold-reader check, and check again after shortening.

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

name: worktree-session-cannot-write-main-checkout
description: "In a desktop-app worktree session a PreToolUse hook refuses Write/Edit to the main checkout; put reports in the worktree root (untracked) and tell Kenneth the path"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 a session running in `.claude/worktrees/<name>` tried to write a report next to its handoff in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/` and the Write tool was refused by a hook: edits to the base checkout "do not land on this session's branch and may corrupt the user's primary working copy". Bash `cp` is not stopped by the hook, but that is working around a deliberate guard, so anything copied there was moved back.

**Why:** handoffs are read from the main checkout ([[handoff-docs-not-committed]]), which makes it tempting to hand the report back in the same place.

**How to apply:** write reports and evidence folders in the worktree root, leave them untracked ([[temp-docs-stay-untracked-and-visible]]), and give Kenneth the worktree path. Never use the scratchpad for a deliverable; the app's file pane cannot open it as part of the project.

description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].

"""Screenshot canvas boards with the canvas's own Design Component runtime, so <dc-import> boards render whole
(render.py draws them blank). Serves <project dir> on a local port with ./support.js = the runtime saved from the
artifact's artifact-type/dc-runtime.js and /_blob/<id> mapped by blobs.json, then runs headless Chrome with its own
--user-data-dir. Usage: render_dc.py <work dir holding project/ and runtime/> <out dir> [--dark] <board.dc.html>..."""
import functools, http.server, json, re, socketserver, subprocess, sys, tempfile, threading
from pathlib import Path
args = sys.argv[1:]
dark = '--dark' in args
if dark: args.remove('--dark')
work, out, names = Path(args[0]), Path(args[1]), args[2:]
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
proj, runtime = work / 'project', work / 'runtime'
blobs = json.loads((runtime / 'blobs.json').read_text()) if (runtime / 'blobs.json').exists() else {}
chrome = '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'
class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def translate_path(self, path):
        p = path.split('?')[0]
        if p.endswith('/support.js'): return str(runtime / 'dc-runtime.js')
        if p.startswith('/_blob/'):
            b = blobs.get(p[7:])
            if b: return str(runtime / b)
        return super().translate_path(path)
    def do_GET(self):
        # --dark: the board's theme prop defaults to dark, the way the canvas's Theme switch sets it.
        if dark and self.path.split('?')[0].endswith('.dc.html') and 'board=1' in self.path:
            s = Path(self.translate_path(self.path)).read_text()
            s = s.replace('"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"light"}', '"theme":{"editor":"enum","options":["light","dark"],"default":"dark"}')
            b = s.encode(); self.send_response(200); self.send_header('Content-Type', 'text/html; charset=utf-8'); self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(b))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b); return
        return super().do_GET()
srv = socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), functools.partial(H, directory=str(proj)))
srv.daemon_threads = True
threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
port = srv.server_address[1]
for name in names:
    s = (proj / name).read_text()
    m = re.search(r'"\$preview":\{"width":(\d+),"height":(\d+)\}', s)
    w, h = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    png = out / (name.replace('.dc.html', '') + ('-dark' if dark else '') + '.png')
    subprocess.run([chrome, '--headless=new', '--disable-gpu', '--no-first-run', f'--user-data-dir={tempfile.mkdtemp()}', '--hide-scrollbars', f'--window-size={w},{h}', '--force-device-scale-factor=2',
                    '--virtual-time-budget=6000', f'--screenshot={png}', f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/{name}?board=1'], check=True, capture_output=True, timeout=90)
    print(png)

---
name: ux-walkthrough-real-app-recipe
description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 33551592-d22c-4161-9a14-9a22ef798541
  modified: 2026-10-28T13:12:42.393Z
---

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].
---
name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.
---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.
---
name: test-datadir-hides-orca-and-v1
description: "first-run test setups: v1 and OrcaSlicer are found in their real folders; no v1 variable (Kenneth had it removed); hide v1 with an empty HOME; a pre-written JusPrin2.conf stops the v1 import"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0bd9fd0b-1fd6-4ed7-9e9b-89af62d57bfb
  modified: 2026-11-07T18:04:39.693Z
---

2026-11-07 Kenneth ran first launch with `--datadir /tmp/JusPrin2-stg` and a pre-written JusPrin2.conf, pressed "Just slice for now", and got the manual printer form instead of the OrcaSlicer import screen. Then OrcaImporter looked for OrcaSlicer beside the data folder, so a /tmp data folder found none.

Since d289298950 / 2ccfeb0a28 on jusprin-newui-integration:
- First launch finds OrcaSlicer and v1 in their default folders, whatever `--datadir` says. `JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL` names the server, so no pre-written conf is needed.
- `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` names another OrcaSlicer folder ("" = none).

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.
